newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares firmer on Svyazinvest auction result.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares firmer on Svyazinvest auction result.

text.p: Leading Russian shares edged up on Friday as dealers focused on the results of the auction of the Svyazinvest telecoms holding, a prominent sale which traders said would ignite a further market rise.
The Russian Trading System index of 22 leading shares rose 2.34 percent to 509.47 on an average $68.62 million in total market volume.

"I think the good news is that the auction did take place," said UFG trader Maxim Perlin. "The price is really good and from now on buyers of regional telecoms and Rostelekom RTKM.RTS will have it in mind. The news will push the market up."

Russian officials said Cyprus-registered company Mustcom, set up by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Russian investment bank Renaissance Capital and others, won 25 percent plus one share in Svyazinvest for $1.875 billion.
Svyazinvest has controlling stakes in 88 regional telecoms and other companies, including Rostelekom long-distance carrier.
Rostelekom rose to $5.05 from $4.71 at Thursday's close, St Petersburg Telephone SPTL.RTS was $2.35 after $2.17, MGTS MGTS.RTS edged up to $2.0 from $1.98.
Perlin said the results of the tender would cause cheaper regional telecoms to rise faster than Rostelekom.
"There are quite a few people wishing to have exposure to Svvyazinvest through regional telecoms," he said.
UCB Corporate Securities Operations Department Head Samit Yakovlev said other shares rose on local operators' speculations but that serious investors remained on the sidelines.
